issues.area: C2 regression from c8f01ca (concurrency/perf at 10,000): the space sweep's follow is counted as one cheap action, so one actor turn follows up to 1,024 jobs
issues.location: Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineJobs.swift:726 (requeue branch: followBeforeActing counted as requeues += 1 under readmissionsPerTurn = 512) and :752 (park branch: followBeforeActing counted as parks += 1 under parksPerPump = 512), in sweepSpaceParked. Reached from EngineTimers.swift:177 (the alarm's .reclaimed sweep after reaped bytes), :372 (.settle) and :389 (a purge's reclaim). The doc comment at EngineJobs.swift:685-691 and the draft's 'C2: at most one follow per action the turn already bounds' (docs/adr-drafts/s3f.md, cycle 4) claim it stays bounded.
issues.problem:
A follow (supersede, re-route each interest, create the new content's job) costs about 10-12 µs per job, which is why followsPerTurn is 256 (EngineFollow.swift:5-10, '256 visits stays near 3 ms'). A re-queue costs about 1 µs and a park about 2 µs. c8f01ca charges each follow as one re-queue or one park, so a single sweep turn now follows up to parksPerPump + readmissionsPerTurn = 1,024 jobs, on top of the sweep's O(n) collection and sort.

PROVEN by PROBE-C4-SWEEP2-C2 (release, -enable-testing), at load 2.8-3.2 (1-min):
- Setup: 10,000 prefetch members alternating 400 and 3,000 bytes, parked awaitingSpace behind a 2,000-byte pending reclaim with 100 bytes of room. A forced sync changes every member's content, and the follow's follow-ups are held. The deletion grace then ends and the alarm's reaper frees the 2,000 bytes. The .reclaimed sweep re-queues the 400-byte members and parks the 3,000-byte ones.
- One handle: heartbeat longest wait 10.18, 10.52 and 10.83 ms, all three over C2. Direct timing of the first sweep turn: 9.28-9.92 ms. That turn did 1,024 follows ('awaiting 10000->8976').
- Two prefetch handles over the same ids (two interests per job): heartbeat 13.62, 14.05 and 13.83 ms; direct 12.92-12.96 ms.
- Same engine and same load without the changed manifest (no follows): heartbeat 6.2-7.3 ms, direct 3.2-3.4 ms.
- At load 8.6-11: the same pattern (10.46-12.59 ms and 13.75-15.04 ms against 6.18-7.28 ms).
- The later follow-up sweep turns are 7.4-12 ms each.
- The .read-only sweep (512 follows per turn) measured 6.2-7.7 ms against 3.3-3.5 ms at load ~40.

The hold seam only makes the interleaving deterministic. In production a reaper or purge sweep can land between the ~40 owned turns of a bounded follow at 10,000. The existing spaceParking and spaceReadmission benchmarks do not cover this, because no follow is owed in them.
issues.fix:
Give the sweep its own follow budget per turn: count each candidate that holdsMovedID against Self.followsPerTurn (256). When the budget is spent, call scheduleSpaceSweepFollowUp(sweep) and break, as the re-queue and park bounds already do.

A verified prototype is at /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronAssetKit/.build-orchestrator/s3f-probes-c4/proto-sweep-follow-budget.diff. With it, at load 3.6-4.2, the probe gives heartbeat 4.91-5.66 ms (one handle) and 6.40-6.54 ms (two handles), and direct 4.2-5.3 ms. The whole Sync bundle passes with it: '✔ Test run with 407 tests in 53 suites passed after 19.561 seconds' (the 405 committed tests plus the two space probes; the committed spaceSweepFollowsTheReplacedContent passes in all 3 cases).

Then:
- Add a BenchSync C2 benchmark of this scenario: a reclaim sweep during an owed follow under a 10,000-member group, re-queueing and parking (S3-R5, c2Budget). VerifyC4CorrectBench.swift's VerifyC4CorrectBench2 is the shape to adapt.
- Add a structural unit test that one sweep turn follows at most followsPerTurn jobs, and show it fails without the budget (S3-R3).
- Correct the C2 sentence in the sweepSpaceParked doc comment and in the draft.

The new blocking issue is a C2 regression that the fix itself introduced (c8f01ca). I proved it at load 2.8-3.2, so load is not the cause. The space sweep now follows each job it re-queues or parks, and each follow counts only as one action against bounds of 512 + 512. One sweep turn can therefore do 1,024 follows. That is 4x followsPerTurn (256), which the code itself sizes at 10-12 µs per visit. At 10,000 members, a reclaim sweep during an owed follow holds the actor 10.2-10.8 ms with one prefetch handle and 13.6-14.1 ms with two handles over the same ids. Without the follow the same sweep takes 6.2-7.3 ms. A prototype follow budget of followsPerTurn per sweep turn brings it to 4.9-6.5 ms, and the whole Sync bundle passes with it.
